verdicts.evidence: Dropping the `^` anchor makes the heading match anywhere on a line. Measured on three fixtures: `####### Territory` (seven hashes), an indented `  ## Territory`, and the prose line `Notes ## Territory` all flip from the structural refusal to a fully read map with a live row — text that is not a heading starts governing files.
verdicts.argument: Dropping the `^` anchor makes the heading match anywhere on a line. Measured on three fixtures: `####### Territory` (seven hashes), an indented `  ## Territory`, and the prose line `Notes ## Territory` all flip from the structural refusal to a fully read map with a live row — text that is not a heading starts governing files.

verdicts.evidence: `\s+` narrowed to `\s` refuses a heading with two spaces. Measured on `##  Territory`: structural goes from null to ``no `Territory` heading`` and the row count from 1 to 0 — the map the operator believes is active is voided, which is the exact near-miss the any-heading-level amendment exists to prevent (CLI diff 33 lines).

verdicts.evidence: `\s*$` inverted to `\S*$` breaks both directions. Measured: `## Territory  ` (trailing spaces, what any editor leaves) stops being read at all, while `## TerritoryX` starts being read as a Territory heading (CLI diff 66 lines).
